title_en: Ma Yanmei v. Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd. — tort dispute

full_text_en:
Ma Yanmei v. Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement

Plaintiff: Ma Yanmei, female, 40 years old, former accountant of the Second Engineering Department of Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd., residing in Chengdong District, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Agents ad litem: Ma Shimin and Qi Hanting, lawyers of Tongguang Law Firm.

Defendant: Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd. Domicile: Qiyi Road, Xining City, Qinghai Province.

Legal representative: Feng Shengshou, chairman and general manager of the company.

Agents ad litem: Gao Meisheng and Chen Xuezhong, lawyers of Huihuang Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Xining City, Qinghai Province, on the grounds of an infringement dispute with the defendant, Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongjian Company).

The plaintiff alleged: Taking advantage of the death of my husband, Qi Zhanlu, the defendant appointed another person to manage a construction engineering team which was jointly established by my husband and me and affiliated with the defendant, but which had independent property and independent operation, thereby seriously infringing upon my lawful rights and interests. I request the court to order the defendant to cease the infringement, return all seized property, and restore my right to operation and management.

The defendant argued: The Second Engineering Department of Qinghai Dongjian Industry & Trade Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Second Department) is a subordinate department of the defendant. After the death of Qi Zhanlu, the head of this department, the defendant needed to conduct an internal settlement with the department. The plaintiff is not the head of this department and cannot interfere with the internal settlement matters of the company. The plaintiff's claim is in essence a matter of inheritance, which can only be resolved after the internal settlement of the company. The defendant has never interfered with the plaintiff's right of inheritance, and there is no fact of infringement. The plaintiff is merely an ordinary citizen; she originally had no right to operation and management, so there is no question of restoring such a right. The plaintiff's claim of infringement is based on an improper cause of action; her request to restore the right to operation and management is based on an improper litigation subject. Therefore, the plaintiff's claims should be dismissed according to law.

The Intermediate People's Court of Xining City, Qinghai Province, found the following facts upon trial:

A construction engineering team established by the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, and her husband, Qi Zhanlu, affiliated with the defendant, Dongjian Company, in May 1998, becoming the Second Department of Dongjian Company. Qi Zhanlu was in charge of the affairs of the Second Department, and Ma Yanmei served as its accountant.

On June 17, 1998, the defendant, Dongjian Company, appointed Qi Zhanlu as the deputy general manager of Dongjian Company and concurrently as the director of the Second Department. In the same year, Qi Zhanlu, in the name of Dongjian Company, entered into construction project contracts with third parties, undertaking three projects: the science and technology cadre residential building of Qinghai Provincial Meteorological Bureau, the comprehensive building of Xining Qizhen Gold Shop, and the comprehensive building of Zhongzhuang Primary School of Chengdong Education Bureau, and organized the Second Department to carry out the construction. In addition, Qi Zhanlu also jointly contracted with Dongjian Company for the Beiguan Street residential building project. To clarify the subordinate relationship of responsibilities, rights, and interests between the company and its various departments for unified management, Dongjian Company signed responsibility target agreements with each department. In the responsibility target agreement signed on March 20, 1999, between Feng Shengshou, the general manager of Dongjian Company, and Qi Zhanlu, the director of the Second Department, Article 3 stipulated: Dongjian Company shall bear legal responsibilities and provide other services for the Second Department; for this, the Second Department shall pay management fees to Dongjian Company. For any construction project secured by the Second Department itself, the department shall pay 6% of the total project cost to the company, including the construction tax; for projects assisted or arranged by the company, the department shall pay 8% of the total project cost; the project funds of the Second Department must be settled through the company's bank account. Article 4 stipulated: The Second Department shall conduct independent accounting economically and assume sole responsibility for its profits and losses. In accordance with the agreement, Qi Zhanlu had paid management fees to Dongjian Company for the projects contracted by the Second Department.

On June 8, 1999, Qi Zhanlu died of illness. On the same day as Qi Zhanlu's death, the defendant, Dongjian Company, appointed Ma Zongyuan, Qi Zhanlu's nephew, to take charge of all work of the Second Department and separately issued notices to the contracting entities of the projects under construction by the Second Department, requiring each entity to remit all economic transactions and project funds arising therefrom to the basic account of Dongjian Company. After Qi Zhanlu's death, the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, repeatedly requested Dongjian Company to allow her to participate in the management of the Second Department but was refused. On June 18, Dongjian Company, in the joint name of itself and the Second Department, issued a notice stating: "Due to the change of project leader of the Second Department, and in order to fulfill the company's legal responsibilities and social credibility, all units and individuals that have economic transactions or creditor-debtor relationships with the Second Department are requested to bring their instruments and relevant documents to our company office for registration and settlement within three months from the date of registration. After the deadline, the responsibility shall be borne by the parties themselves, and our company shall not be liable." After this notice was published in the Qinghai Daily on June 23, Ma Yanmei wrote to Dongjian Company, pointing out that Dongjian Company, without the knowledge and presence of the property owner, unilaterally disposed of the affairs of the Second Department and refused to allow her to participate in the management of the Second Department's property, which constituted interference in the specific affairs of the Second Department and an infringement of the property rights of the property owner. Dongjian Company ignored Ma Yanmei's opinion, and Ma Yanmei therefore filed a lawsuit with the court.

It was further found that after the construction team established by the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, and her husband affiliated with the defendant, Dongjian Company, a total of six vehicles, including a Dongfeng brand dump truck, a flatbed truck, a Chang'an brand single-row cab truck, and a Santana sedan, were transferred into the name of Dongjian Company. Among these six vehicles, only the Chang'an brand single-row cab truck was in Ma Yanmei's possession; the remaining five were all at the construction sites of the Second Department. In addition, a Toyota minibus, which belonged to Ma Yanmei and her husband and had not been transferred to Dongjian Company, was also at a construction site of the Second Department. As of March 8, 1999, various items such as mixers, headframes, hoists, mud pumps, electric saws, vibrators, air compressors, electric welders, oxygen cylinders, acetylene cylinders, threading machines, rebar benders, cutters, terrazzo grinders, tampers, manual hoists, levels, theodolites, pipe benders, pressure pumps, cutters, impact drills, electric drills, trolleys, drainage pipes, desks, chairs, filing cabinets, bed boards, scaffolding boards, steel scaffolding poles, steel clamps, steel formwork, and other property at the various construction sites of the Second Department were all registered in the name of Qi Zhanlu. After March 8, there were also accounting records for property purchased, including mortar mixers, welded pipes, plugs, corner molds, and steel formwork. A material yard leased by the Second Department in the name of Dongjian Company contained property entirely owned by the Second Department.

The Intermediate People's Court of Xining City, Qinghai Province, held that:

Although the Second Department was affiliated with the defendant, Dongjian Company, Dongjian Company had never made any investment in the Second Department. All the property under the name of the Second Department originated from the community property of the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, and her husband, Qi Zhanlu. According to the agreement between Dongjian Company and Qi Zhanlu, the director of the Second Department, the Second Department conducted independent accounting and assumed sole responsibility for its profits and losses within Dongjian Company, and in its operations, it undertook projects in the name of Dongjian Company externally, for which the Second Department was obliged to pay management fees to Dongjian Company. This indicates that Qi Zhanlu had not transferred the ownership of the Second Department's property to Dongjian Company and entrusted the company with its operation and management; nor had Dongjian Company, which had the right to operate in the construction industry, ever obtained the right to dispose of the Second Department's property, but instead permitted the Second Department to operate relatively independently within the company using its own property.

The term "operation" refers to the production or marketing activities organized by an operator through the deployment and use of its own human, material, and financial resources, or those legally managed by it, in order to achieve the expected profit-making purpose. It can be seen that where the defendant, Dongjian Company, had never obtained the right to dispose of the Second Department's property, even if it held a lawful operating status, it could not conduct business activities by deploying or using the property of others. After Qi Zhanlu's death, only the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, as one of the co-owners of the community property, and the other heirs of Qi Zhanlu had the right to dispose of the property of the Second Department. Dongjian Company could only directly exercise the right to operation and management of the Second Department with the consent and authorization of these persons. By taking advantage of the affiliation management, Dongjian Company arbitrarily appointed another person to take charge of the work of the Second Department after Qi Zhanlu's death and issued notices and published announcements to settle the Second Department's claims and debts; this was an act beyond its authority and infringed upon the ownership rights of the property owners.

During his lifetime, through the contract with the defendant, Dongjian Company, Qi Zhanlu obtained the right to operate relatively independently within Dongjian Company, which held the business operation right. However, this right could not exist independently of Dongjian Company's business operation right. The acquisition of a business operation right requires certain qualifications and approval. The plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, had never become a subject entitled to the business operation right in the construction industry; therefore, her claim for restoration of the right to operation and management is erroneous and cannot be upheld.

Article 71 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "Property ownership means the owner's rights to lawfully possess, use, profit from, and dispose of his own property." After Qi Zhanlu's death, Ma Yanmei, as a co-owner of the property and co-operator, had the right to continue to operate the affairs of the Second Department relatively independently within Dongjian Company in accordance with the original agreement, and Dongjian Company should cooperate. If the parties could no longer maintain this relationship, it should also be terminated through equal negotiation. Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Xining City rendered the following judgment:

The defendant, Dongjian Company, shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, deliver to the plaintiff, Ma Yanmei, the financial accounts of the Second Department, the assets in the material yard, all materials relating to the projects (including jointly constructed projects) undertaken by the Second Department, and the accounting records for the purchase of materials.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 24,535 shall be borne by the defendant, Dongjian Company.

Dongjian Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the High People's Court of Qinghai Province. The grounds for appeal were: The company had invested human and material resources in the management of the Second Department. Moreover, the Second Department, by contracting projects in the company's name, still owed debts to others, and creditors had repeatedly demanded payment from the company. It was impossible to hand over the Second Department to Ma Yanmei without first settling accounts under these circumstances. Ma Yanmei and the children of Qi Zhanlu only had the right of inheritance in the property and should not interfere in operational matters. The first-instance judgment failed to consider the liabilities of the Second Department, the facts were unclear, and the judgment should be reversed. Ma Yanmei argued that the first-instance judgment had clearly found the facts and correctly applied the law, and should be upheld.

Upon trial, the High People's Court of Qinghai Province held that the facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear, and the evidence was credible and sufficient.

The property of the Second Department was the community property of the appellee, Ma Yanmei, and her husband, which was not disputed by the parties. The Second Department was affiliated with the appellant, Dongjian Company. Although Dongjian Company had invested human and material resources in management, this was not an investment and could not entitle it to obtain direct right to operation and management of the Second Department; moreover, Dongjian Company's input in this regard had been compensated by the management fees paid by the Second Department. During Qi Zhanlu's lifetime, the affairs of the Second Department were jointly operated by Ma Yanmei and her husband relatively independently within Dongjian Company. The claims and debts of the Second Department with third parties during Qi Zhanlu's lifetime were, according to the agreement between Dongjian Company and the Second Department, always handled by the Second Department itself. Ma Yanmei was aware of this and was also obligated to repay the debts of the Second Department. It was only after Qi Zhanlu's death that Dongjian Company arbitrarily appointed another person to preside over the affairs of the Second Department and issued a notice to handle the Second Department's claims and debts, refusing to allow Ma Yanmei to manage the Second Department, which made the debts of the Second Department impossible to determine, and creditors successively approached Dongjian Company for repayment. This was the inevitable result of Dongjian Company's infringement of the ownership rights of the Second Department's property. The appellant's appeal based on this ground cannot be sustained. The first-instance judgment correctly applied the law and the decision was appropriate. Accordingly, the High People's Court of Qinghai Province rendered the following judgment on February 22, 2000:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 24,535 shall be borne by the appellant, Dongjian Company.
